marker: # unit_length and ref_repeats are Table 3 and Table 1 of Matamoros et
# al. 2011: Table 3 gives the consensus repeat unit and its length, and Table 1 gives the NCC2705 MLVA
# profile, 6-4-3-7-16 in this locus order. ref_size is the product these primers give in the NCC2705
# assembly GCA_000007525.1, which lies inside the published size range of every locus. A run on
# NCC2705 returns the published profile with a residual of zero at every locus. VNTR12 can take a half
# repeat allele, 2.5 or 5.5, as the paper notes; NCC2705 is a whole 6.
# patterns is N/A at every locus: counting the published consensus motif in the NCC2705 amplicon does
# not return the published copy number at any of the five, because the arrays are imperfect and the
# flank carries partial motifs, so a stored pattern would raise a false COUNT_DISAGREES. The motifs
# VNTR23 does not use the published copy number of 3. With 3 the implied flank is 374 - 3 x 10 = 344 bp,
# but products of 314 bp occur, which is shorter than the flank alone and therefore impossible, and 12 of
# 20 genomes screened got a negative allele. The NCC2705 amplicon holds 6 copies of the published 10 bp
# unit exactly and 7 counted with one mismatch; ref_repeats is 7, the count at the mismatch allowance the
# scheme runs with, which leaves a 304 bp flank against 41 bp of primers and makes every allele seen
# positive. Alleles at VNTR23 are therefore 4 higher than the published numbering; subtract 4 to compare
# with published VNTR23 values. The reference product, 374 bp, is also 1 bp above the top of the size
# range Table 2 gives for this locus (313-373 bp), so the published sizes and numbering for VNTR23 may
# rest on a different scale; reconcile them against the paper before comparing whole profiles.
# from Table 3 are recorded here instead: VNTR12 TCGTGGGTAGCAAC, VNTR21 AGCCGAATC, VNTR23 CTGATATTCG,
# VNTR25 CACAACCTGTTT, VNTR26 AGCCATATCA.
